/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 74-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of shortness of breath and leg swelling. He has trouble climbing one flight of stairs due to dyspnea. He has hypertension and was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 6 months ago. Current medications include hydrochlorothiazide. Cardiopulmonary examination shows jugular venous distention, bibasilar crackles, and pitting edema in the lower extremities. Transthoracic echocardiography shows a thickened myocardium with elevated diastolic filling pressures. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism of this patient's cardiomyopathy?

Options:
A. Chronic vasoconstriction
B. Myosin gene mutation
C. Amyloid deposition
D. Chronic hypercalcemia
E. Iron deposition

text: {"in_scope": false, "reason": "The question pertains to cardiac pathophysiology and cardiomyopathy, which is outside the scope of psychiatry and mental health."}
